data.title: Java security flaw explained: Why CISA, CERT-In urge urgent software update
data.description:
Java, a programming languages used for building software and running online services, is facing a critical security flaw that could put sensitive systems at risk. Called Java4Shell, the vulnerability could allow hackers to access information stored by applications or run malicious code on affected systems. Discovered by cybersecurity researchers at Calif on November 17, the flaw has prompted urgent advisories from security agencies in the US and India. It is tracked as CVE-2026-114938 and affects OpenJDK, the open-source implementation of Java used by several software vendors.
 
Oracle, which owns the Java trademark, released a patch on Tuesday, as did OpenJDK. Since several vendors build their Java distributions on OpenJDK, their users could also be affected.
 

What is Java and where is it used

Java is a programming language used to build applications and software for computers, servers and other devices. It is widely used in business software, websites, mobile apps and games. For example, when someone logs in to a banking website, Java may be used in the backend systems to check login details, process transactions and communicate with databases. It also supports services such as managing user accounts and handling data, even though users may not see it working.
 
Java can run on different operating systems and devices, which makes it useful for building software used across computers and servers. When a Java programme is created, it is converted into a format called bytecode, which is then run by a component known as the Java Virtual Machine (JVM). The JVM helps the same programme work on different systems without developers having to rewrite it for each one. The Java Development Kit (JDK) provides the tools needed to build Java applications, while OpenJDK is its open-source version. Several technology companies use OpenJDK to create their own Java software, which means a security flaw in its code can affect products from multiple vendors. 
ALSO READ: Sarvam faces backlash for offering Chinese AI models on its platform

What is the Java4Shell flaw

Java4Shell is a memory-corruption flaw in a part of OpenJDK that decodes Base64 data. Base64 is a common method of converting computer data into text made up of letters, numbers and symbols. It is used in different applications and online processes, including some ways of handling login information and file uploads.
 
According to Calif, the cybersecurity company that disclosed the flaw on November 17, the problem is in an optimised version of the Base64 decoder. The code is designed to process data faster on certain Intel and AMD processors. However, when it receives specially prepared input, it can write data beyond the memory space set aside for it. This can damage other information that the application is holding.
 
This type of error is called memory corruption. So basically, a programme is supposed to put information in one part of memory but ends up overwriting information stored next to it. An attacker may be able to use this error to read sensitive data, such as passwords, access keys or session tokens.
 
Under certain conditions, the flaw could also allow remote code execution (RCE). This means an attacker could make a computer or server run commands without having normal access to it. CISA warned that specially crafted Base64 input could crash the JVM and potentially allow an attacker to execute code remotely without authentication.
 
The vulnerability does not affect every computer running Java. According to Calif and other security advisories, exploitation depends on the Java version, the application and the processor. The issue concerns certain x86-64 systems that support AVX-512 VBMI instructions, which are specialised instructions used by some processors to speed up data processing. ARM64 systems are not affected by this particular issue. 
ALSO READ: Google Play names best apps and games of 2026: Here are Indian apps in list

How did researchers find it

Calif said its researcher Quang Luong used OpenAI's Codex to examine OpenJDK code. The AI tool pointed to a possible problem in the Base64 decoder. Luong then investigated the suggestion, tested the code and developed a proof of concept.
 
A proof of concept is a demonstration that a security flaw can be triggered. It does not mean attackers have used it in real-world incidents. According to Calif, it took about an hour to identify the vulnerability and another two hours to develop the first working exploit.
 
The researchers also used a technique called heap grooming. The Java heap is an area of memory where an application stores information while it is running. Heap grooming involves influencing how that information is arranged so that a memory error can affect data an attacker wants to reach. Calif said this helped researchers demonstrate how the flaw could be used to expose memory and, in some test cases, run code.
 
Calif tested the vulnerability against several widely used products, including Keycloak, Atlassian Jira, Confluence, Jenkins, JFrog Artifactory and PingFederate. The company said its tests demonstrated remote code execution without authentication in some configurations. Other products, including Apache Kafka, Apache Solr and Elasticsearch, required an attacker to be logged in for the demonstrations. These results do not mean every installation of these products is vulnerable or has been compromised.
 
The discovery is another example of AI being used in cybersecurity research. AI tools can help researchers examine large amounts of code and identify areas that need closer inspection. 
ALSO READ: Google Play names best apps and games of 2026: Here are Indian apps in list

Why have security agencies issued urgent advisories

US-based Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) issued an alert on November 17, urging organisations to patch the vulnerability. It advised them to check their software inventories for Java Development Kits and Java runtimes, including versions bundled inside other applications, container images and devices. A container is a package that includes an application and the components it needs to run. Such bundled Java versions may not appear as separate software entries, making them harder for IT teams to identify.
 
CISA said organisations should apply vendor updates as soon as possible, giving priority to systems that can be accessed over the internet. If an organisation cannot patch immediately, it should restrict access to affected services, validate incoming Base64 data and monitor for unusual Java processes or unexpected crashes. These are temporary steps and do not replace installing the security update.
 
India's CERT-In issued its advisory on November 18. It warned that a remote attacker could send a specially crafted request containing malformed Base64 data and potentially execute code on a vulnerable system. CERT-In advised organisations and individuals using affected Oracle Java SE and Oracle GraalVM products to apply the updates provided by Oracle.
 
Oracle published its November 2026 security update on November 17, listing CVE-2026-114938 among the vulnerabilities addressed. The OpenJDK project also issued an advisory. Other vendors are handling updates for their own Java distributions, including Amazon Corretto and Red Hat builds. Organisations using distributions such as Eclipse Temurin, Microsoft Build of OpenJDK, Azul Zulu, BellSoft Liberica and SAP SapMachine should check the relevant vendor guidance rather than assume that an Oracle update automatically fixes every installation.
 
The Canadian Centre for Cyber Security and the European Union's CERT-EU have also advised organisations to identify affected systems and install updates. CERT-EU has recommended prioritising applications accessible over the internet. These warnings reflect the fact that Java is used across many organisations and that the vulnerable code is shared by different Java distributions.

How is Java4Shell different from PHP2Shell

Java4Shell follows a separate discovery by Calif involving PHP, another programming language used to build websites and web applications. The earlier vulnerabilities, referred to as PHP2Shell, could allow attackers to execute commands on affected servers. Both cases involved AI-assisted research and prompted organisations to review and update vulnerable software.
 
The key difference is the reach of the software involved. PHP is widely used in websites and web applications. Java is also used for online services, but it is found in a broader range of enterprise and backend systems, including identity management, banking, cloud services and other business applications. A flaw in OpenJDK can therefore affect products from several vendors that rely on the same underlying code.
 
There is no confirmed evidence in the cited advisories that Java4Shell has been used in real-world attacks. However, the technical details are public, researchers have demonstrated ways to trigger the flaw, and security agencies have urged organisations not to delay updates. The immediate task for IT teams is to find every Java installation, including runtimes bundled inside other products, check whether it is affected and install the appropriate vendor patch.

Have there been similar security incidents involving Java before

Java has faced major security vulnerabilities before. In December 2021, a flaw known as Log4Shell was discovered in Apache Log4j, a logging library used by many Java applications. Tracked as CVE-2021-44228, it could allow attackers to run malicious code remotely by sending specially crafted requests to vulnerable systems. In March 2022, another flaw, called Spring4Shell, was found in the Spring Framework, which is used to develop Java applications. It could also enable remote code execution under specific conditions. Both incidents prompted security agencies to urge organisations to identify affected software and install patches.
 
A more recent example is PHP2Shell, disclosed in October 2026. It involved two vulnerabilities in PHP, a programming language widely used to build websites and web applications, which could allow attackers to execute malicious code on affected web servers without authentication. The US National Security Agency issued an advisory on October 21, urging organisations to patch vulnerable systems or take them offline if updates could not be applied immediately. In India, CERT-In issued a separate advisory on PHP2Shell on October 22, specifically warning micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs).
 
For Java4Shell, CERT-In issued an advisory on November 18, warning Indian organisations and individuals using affected Oracle Java SE and GraalVM versions about the risk of remote code execution.

data.title: Missed ITR deadline? You may claim Section 54 capital gains tax relief
data.description:
In a recent ruling in Margaret Smith v. Deputy Commissioner of Income Tax (International Taxation), the Jaipur Bench of the Income Tax Appellate Tribunal (ITAT) held that the tax department cannot deny a taxpayer the capital gains tax exemption under Section 54 of the Income-tax Act solely because the taxpayer missed the deadline for filing the original income tax return (ITR), provided the taxpayer meets the substantive conditions for the exemption. 
In the case, a taxpayer sold her old residential flat for ₹62.27 lakh and invested the entire sale proceeds in another residential property within the stipulated period. However, the Income Tax Department denied her Section 54 exemption because she had not filed her original return and claimed the relief only in her response to a reassessment notice under Section 148. The ITAT held that filing the ITR on time is not an independent condition under Section 54, particularly when the taxpayer has already invested the entire capital gain in the new property. 
 
Section 54 relief and ITR filing 
Section 54 exempts long-term capital gains (LTCG) from the sale of a residential house if the taxpayer reinvests the gains in another house in India within the prescribed period. “The new property must be purchased within one year before or two years after the sale, or constructed within three years. The exemption generally covers one house, with a one-time option to invest in two houses if the capital gain does not exceed ₹2 crore,” says Vishwas Panjiar, managing partner, SVAS Business Advisors.
The key takeaway for taxpayers from this case is that a procedural lapse in filing the return does not automatically disqualify a taxpayer from Section 54 relief if the taxpayer meets the substantive conditions. “However, the ruling does not waive the obligation to file returns on time or provide a blanket relaxation of tax-filing deadlines. Taxpayers should continue to meet their filing obligations and retain evidence of property transactions and investments,” says Panjiar. 
Who can claim Section 54 relief 
Before they claim Section 54 relief, taxpayers should verify that they held the original residential house for more than 24 months and that they qualify for the exemption. They must buy a replacement house in India within one year before or two years after the sale, or build one within three years of the sale.  
“It is also important to distinguish Section 54 from Section 54F. While Section 54 applies to the sale of a residential house, Section 54F apply when assets such as vacant land or commercial property are sold and the proceeds are invested in a residential house, subject to additional conditions. Incorrect classification can result in denial or reduction of the exemption and an additional tax liability,” says Panjiar. 
Calculating the exemption 
The Section 54 exemption is the lower of the LTCG arising from the sale of the original house and the eligible investment in the new residential property. Taxpayers must calculate the exemption on the capital gain, not the total sale proceeds. A ₹10 crore ceiling applies to the eligible investment. For instance, if the gain is ₹60 lakh and the investment is ₹45 lakh, the exemption is ₹45 lakh. If the investment is ₹70 lakh, the entire ₹60 lakh gain may be exempt, subject to other conditions. 
According to Panjiar, if taxpayers have yet to invest the full amount when they file the return, they must deposit the unutilised gain under the Capital Gains Accounts Scheme (CGAS) by the applicable ITR due date and use it within the prescribed period. Any unused amount becomes taxable after that period. A sale of the new property within three years can also affect the earlier exemption. 
Builder delays 
Taxpayers must build the new house within three years of the sale. They should document delays by the builder. Courts have granted relief in certain cases where taxpayers demonstrated genuine investment and timely payments but possession was delayed for reasons beyond their control. However, this is not an automatic extension of the deadline. “Taxpayers should preserve the builder-buyer agreement, allotment letter, payment receipts, bank statements and correspondence with the developer to establish that the investment was genuine and the delay was attributable to the builder,” says Panjiar. 
Home loans, gifts and family contributions 
A home loan to buy a new residential property does not, by itself, disqualify a taxpayer from Section 54 relief. Similarly, taxpayers can use genuine monetary gifts from specified relatives towards the purchase, provided they meet the other conditions for the exemption. 
“Taxpayers should retain the sale deed of the old property, purchase documents of the new house, bank statements, home loan sanction and disbursement records, and payment receipts. Where family gifts are involved, they should also maintain the gift deed, bank transfer records and evidence of the donor’s financial capacity. These documents help establish the investment and its source,” says Neeraj Agarwala, senior partner, Nangia & Co. 
Precautions for joint property purchases 
Ideally, taxpayers who claim the Section 54 exemption should register the new property in their own name. However, courts have allowed relief in several cases where taxpayers bought the property jointly with a spouse, particularly when they could establish that the investment came from their own funds. 
“The position may be less certain when the property is registered exclusively in the name of parents, siblings or other relatives. Such claims could invite litigation. Taxpayers should clearly document ownership shares, individual contributions and the source of funds through registered property documents and bank records. The same investment should not be used to claim exemption twice,” says Agarwala. 
Documents to retain 
Taxpayers should preserve all relevant property documents, including the registered sale and purchase deeds, allotment letter, builder-buyer agreement and possession letter. They should also retain bank statements, loan statements and payment receipts to establish the cost of acquisition. 
“Where the property was purchased through instalments, the payment schedule should be retained as well. In cases of inheritance or gift, the taxpayer should preserve a copy of the will or gift deed, along with the previous owner’s documents establishing the original cost and date of acquisition,” says Rupali Singhania, partner, Areete Consultants. 
How to report sale in ITR 
Taxpayers must report the capital gains from the sale of the original residential property and the Section 54 exemption they claim for the investment in a new residential house in the Capital Gains schedule (Schedule CG) of the ITR. “If the taxpayer misses claiming the exemption while filing the original return, the claim can be made by filing a revised return within the prescribed time limit,” says Singhania.
Mistakes to avoid while claiming Section 54 
•    Not depositing unutilised capital gains by ITR due date
•    Parking money in a regular savings or fixed deposit account instead of designated CGAS account
•    Failing to deposit entire unutilised capital gain
•    Not using the money to buy or construct a house within prescribed period
•    Not retaining payment receipts, bank statements and property-related documents as proof of investment 
Source: Nangia & Co  
 The writer is a Delhi-based independent journalist

data.title: SAMIL rises 4% on volume surge, Korea unit liquidation; Geojit keeps 'Buy'
data.description:
Shares of Samvardhana Motherson International Ltd (SAMIL) traded higher on Thursday, supported by strong volumes and the company's announcement regarding the liquidation of its South Korean subsidiary.
 
The stock opened on a flat note at ₹156.55 but soon gained momentum, rising to an intraday high of ₹163.90 on the BSE, up nearly 4.5 per cent.
 
The rally was accompanied by a sharp surge in trading volumes. As of 2:30  PM, the stock was trading 4 per cent higher at ₹163.70, with a spurt in volume by more than 9.27 times versus the two-week average traded quantity of 1.8 million.  Samvardhana Motherson liquidates South Korea unit
 
 
Notably, Samvardhana Motherson International has informed through a filing that upon submission of an application by MSSL Korea WH Limited, South Korea (MSSL Korea), an indirect wholly owned subsidiary of the company, the Registry Division of the Cheongju District Court, Republic of Korea, has approved liquidation of MSSL Korea vide certificate of dissolution dated November 18, 2026. 
 
MSSL Korea was incorporated on November 27, 2012. It was not carrying out any business or operations, and thus the members of MSSL Korea approved its dissolution on August 20, 2026.
 
The income and net worth of MSSL Korea during the financial year 2025-26 were KRW 112.59 million (equivalent to ₹7.09 million) and KRW (1,121.46) million (equivalent to ₹(70.61) million), respectively. Further, the income of MSSL Korea contributed ‘negligible’ to the consolidated revenue and consolidated net worth of the company as at the end of the financial year 2025-26.  
Samvardhana Motherson share price target  
Meanwhile, Geojit has maintained its 'Buy' rating on Samvardhana Motherson International and revised its target to ₹190. The target implies an upside of more than 20 per cent from the previous close of ₹157.
 
The brokerage said that Samvardhana Motherson International delivered another strong quarter (Q2FY27) supported by robust revenue growth, healthy profitability and successful integration of Autoelectric and Yutaka Giken. 
 
Its PAT rose 44 per cent Y-o-Y to ₹1,218 crore, while consolidated revenue rose 26.9 per cent Y-o-Y to ₹38,280 crore, supported by the consolidation of Autoelectric and Yutaka Giken as well as strong demand for wiring harnesses division. The wiring harness division remained the key growth engine, with revenue increasing 68.2 per cent Y-o-Y to ₹14,382 crore.
 
Ebitda in Q2 rose 28.6 per cent Y-o-Y to ₹3,357 crore. Margin remained broadly stable at 8.8 per cent (up 10bps YoY), despite the consolidation of newly acquired businesses operating at lower profitability levels. 
 
The company’s booked business rose to a record USD 106 billion, providing strong revenue visibility, while the scale-up of non-automotive businesses such as aerospace and consumer electronics is gradually improving diversification. A disciplined capital allocation framework, comfortable leverage profile and continued focus on automation and operational efficiency support sustainable earnings growth, the brokerage said.
 
"Strong order visibility, customer diversification and rising content per vehicle remain key structural drivers," Geojit added. 
Disclaimer: Views and outlook in this report belong to the brokerages and analysts cited. They do not reflect the views of Business Standard. Readers are advised to exercise discretion.

data.title: Jaishankar flags 'weaponisation' of resources at India-Japan 2+2 talks
data.description:
External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar on Thursday flagged the growing "weaponisation" of connectivity, resources and supply chains, and called for stronger India-Japan cooperation amid global uncertainty and a complex Indo-Pacific strategic landscape.

Jaishankar and Defence Minister Rajnath Singh are in Tokyo for the fourth India-Japan Foreign and Defence Ministers' Dialogue, known as the 2+2 meeting, held on Thursday.

Addressing the media after the 2+2 meeting, Jaishankar said the global order was facing multiple shocks, including two major ongoing conflicts, economic volatility and the after-effects of the Covid-19 pandemic.

"There are two major ongoing conflicts whose impact have been felt even in distant regions," he said, adding that these developments had heightened concerns over energy, trade, food and health security.

 

"As we seek to secure ourselves on these fronts, trusted and substantive partnerships like ours become more valuable," the minister said.

The Russia-Ukraine war and the conflict in West Asia have had repercussions far beyond their respective regions, affecting global energy markets, maritime shipping and food security.

Jaishankar said New Delhi and Tokyo were committed to keeping the Indo-Pacific free and open, and were joined in that endeavour by other Quad partners.

The remarks came two days after Prime Minister Narendra Modi, US President Donald Trump, Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi and Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese met in Manila for a Quad leaders' summit.

"The reality is that old assumptions may no longer hold true and each one of us will have to make a greater contribution to global good," Jaishankar said, adding that such contributions could come through initiatives and activities at the national and bilateral levels or with like-minded partners.

"We also spoke about a growing tendency to weaponise connectivity, resources, services, supply chains and market shares," said the minister, adding that many of these had direct implications for national security.

"Strengthening resilience and exploring new options must be seen in that context," he said.

Jaishankar also referred to growing concerns over connectivity and chokepoints in the light of experiences in the Gulf, stressing the importance of ensuring the smooth functioning of maritime trade.

"Ensuring that maritime trade, which is at the heart of international commerce, functions smoothly is imperative. Our maritime cooperation can help make a difference," he said, adding that discussions on the subject were particularly timely.

The two sides also agreed on the importance of adhering to international law in this context, he said.

The 2+2 meeting also took into account the changing nature of warfare, with Jaishankar pointing to the effective application of smart weapons and innovative solutions.

"Our cooperation here feeds into a larger engagement on innovation and startups," the minister said.

Jaishankar said the broader objective of India-Japan cooperation was to support a multipolar Asia and a multipolar world, adding that the two countries had been strong proponents of reformed multilateralism.

"We are two significant nations of the Indo-Pacific with a long and continuous history of friendship and goodwill," he said, adding that a stronger India-Japan relationship could play a more important role as countries entered an era in which each had to step up its contributions to the global order.

"Our 2+2 discussions today and the understandings we reached were a very good step in that direction," he said.

The 2+2 format brings together the foreign and defence ministers of both countries to review their strategic relationship and discuss regional and global security challenges.

On Wednesday, Jaishankar addressed the Raisina Tokyo Dialogue, where he identified five defining features of the changing global landscape, including repeated shocks to the international system, the weaponisation of economic activity, greater risk-taking, de-risking and diversification, and the growing importance of trusted partnerships.

data.title: Grand Theft Auto 6: New Vice City, record viewership, and global frenzy
data.description:
More than a decade after Grand Theft Auto V, Rockstar Games has release a new chapter called the Grand Theft Auto 6, bringing players back to Vice City in a new open-world adventure centred on two protagonists, Jason Duval and Lucia Caminos. The launch has drawn millions of viewers to gaming livestreams, received near-perfect scores from critics and attracted attention beyond the gaming community. While some players have reported glitches and technical issues, the initial response suggests that GTA 6 has made a strong start. Here is a look at the gameplay experience and how the game has been received globally.
 

First impression: A different kind of GTA experience

GTA 6 does not take long to establish its setting or introduce the relationship at the centre of its story. The opening begins in Vice City, two years before the main events. Jason Duval finds himself in a tense encounter with Lucia Caminos, who confronts him over a car. The situation escalates, bringing the police into the picture and forcing the two to work together to get away.
Screenshot from GTA 6 opening sequence
The sequence then moves into a stylised introduction, with illustrations, music and glimpses of Vice City's nightlife, beaches and neon-lit skyline. It also offers an early look at the growing relationship between the two protagonists before revealing that Lucia is in prison. The story subsequently moves forward to nine months before the opening events, setting up the circumstances in which the main narrative begins. Also Read | Get GTA 6 in minutes: Blinkit rolls out quick delivery in 11 cities
 
The opening is relatively brief, but it establishes an important difference from GTA V. While the earlier game introduced three protagonists whose individual stories eventually converged, GTA 6 builds its narrative around a partnership. Jason and Lucia are not simply two characters players can switch between. Their relationship, conversations and shared criminal pursuits are central to the experience.
Vice City in GTA 6 (Screenshot)
The early part of the game takes a little time to build momentum. Rather than immediately moving into elaborate heists, it introduces the characters' circumstances and their connections with people in Leonida's criminal underworld. The initial jobs help establish how the pair operate together and provide a gradual introduction to the game's world and mechanics.
 
The change in emphasis is noticeable when compared with GTA V. The earlier game frequently moved between Michael, Franklin and Trevor, using their contrasting personalities and criminal activities to drive the story. GTA 6 is more invested in the dynamic between Jason and Lucia. Their conversations during drives, time spent together away from missions and reactions to events give the narrative a more personal dimension. 
ALSO READ: GTA 6 India launch: First impressions, prices, editions and download size

A more detailed world to explore

The biggest early impression comes from the world itself. Vice City and the wider Leonida setting are designed to feel occupied even when players are not following a mission. Pedestrians have their own conversations and reactions, traffic fills the roads, and unexpected incidents can interrupt an otherwise routine journey.
 
The level of environmental detail is particularly noticeable. The game uses lighting, reflections, weather and character animations to make locations feel more lived-in. Vice City's neon-lit streets and nightlife offer a different atmosphere from its coastal surroundings, while the wider state includes rural areas, waterways and smaller settlements.
Screenshot from GTA 6 Chapter 1
This is also where GTA 6 appears to move beyond the approach taken in GTA V. The earlier game offered a large and varied map, but the new instalment puts greater emphasis on activity and detail within individual locations. There are also small environmental touches, incidental encounters and everyday activities that can keep players occupied outside the main story.
 
There is also a contrast between the game's criminal missions and the ordinary activities available to Jason and Lucia. Alongside robberies, shootouts and police pursuits, players can spend time fishing, hunting, racing, visiting gyms and exploring the city. The game moves between action-heavy sequences and quieter moments involving everyday activities, giving the relationship between the two protagonists more room to develop.
 
The visual presentation is another noticeable step forward. The city looks different depending on the time of day, while rain, reflections and changing light add detail to roads, vehicles and buildings. Character models and animations are also more detailed, with the behaviour of pedestrians contributing to the sense of activity around the player.
Jason Duval and Lucia Caminos in GTA 6 (Screenshot)
The controls can feel cumbersome at times, and the campaign takes a while to pick up pace. The opening chapters spend considerable time introducing the characters, their circumstances and the game's mechanics. For players expecting the pace of GTA V's more explosive missions from the outset, GTA 6 may require some patience.
 
But its early hours make clear that Rockstar is attempting more than a visual upgrade to the previous game. The focus on Jason and Lucia, the more involved world and the contrast between criminal activity and everyday life give GTA 6 a different narrative and gameplay rhythm.

GTA 6 launch draws record global audience

The scale of GTA 6's launch became evident within hours of its global rollout. Players across markets began streaming their first experiences of Vice City, while gaming audiences tuned in to watch creators explore the game and share their reactions.
 
According to livestreaming analytics platform Streams Charts, GTA 6 attracted more than 7.18 million concurrent viewers across Twitch, YouTube and Kick during its initial launch period. The figure made it the biggest video game launch on livestreaming platforms tracked by the firm. On Twitch alone, the game crossed 3.29 million concurrent viewers, surpassing the platform's previous record for a game category, held by Fortnite.
 
The launch also drew large audiences to individual gaming channels. Spanish streamer Rubius attracted around 311,000 concurrent viewers within an hour of starting his broadcast, according to Twitch. Indian gaming creator Mythpat was among the leading streamers globally, recording a peak audience of more than 125,000 viewers, according to Streams Charts.
ALSO READ: Grand Theft Auto VI wins rave reviews as gamers return to Vice City
The commercial response has been similarly significant. Analytics firm Sensor Tower estimated that GTA 6 had sold more than 17 million copies, generating over $1.65 billion in revenue by November 19. These are third-party estimates and have not been independently confirmed by Rockstar Games. The figures nevertheless indicate the scale of the game's initial demand.
 
The launch has also extended beyond gaming communities. In India, Prime Minister Narendra Modi shared social media content inspired by the Grand Theft Auto franchise on November 19. Consumer electronics brand boAt offered employees an optional day off to mark the release, encouraging them to spend the day playing the game.
 

Logging off to lock in ???? https://t.co/0Afoc3juIN

— Miami HEAT (@MiamiHEAT) November 19, 2026
In Miami, the NBA's Miami Heat marked the occasion with a Vice City-themed match against the Milwaukee Bucks. The court and stadium featured the game's familiar neon pink and blue colours, reflecting the cultural reach of a release that has extended beyond the video game industry.
 
The response has also been visible at gaming events and launch gatherings, with players in cities such as London and Sydney attending midnight celebrations.

Critics give GTA 6 near-perfect reviews

The early critical reception has been overwhelmingly positive. GTA 6 received a Metascore of 99 out of 100 on review aggregator Metacritic, placing it alongside Nintendo's The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time, which has held the same score since 1998. The aggregate score is subject to change as more reviews are added.
 
Several prominent gaming publications awarded the title their highest ratings. IGN gave it 10 out of 10, with reviewer Luke Reilly describing it as the single most impressive video game he had played. The Guardian, Eurogamer and GamesRadar+ awarded it five stars, while GameSpot and Game Informer also gave it perfect scores.
 
The reviews have particularly highlighted the detail in Leonida's open world and the relationship between Jason and Lucia. The Guardian's Keza MacDonald noted that the relationship between the two protagonists gave the narrative an emotional dimension that was not necessarily expected from the franchise. Bloomberg journalist Jason Schreier also described the game as a masterpiece.
 
The Washington Post awarded the game four stars, praising its portrayal of human behaviour and the interactions between its non-playable characters. While the early reviews have been largely positive, some critics have pointed to aspects such as the controls and the pacing of certain sections.

Players report glitches and technical issues

The launch has not been entirely free of technical problems. While the early critical response has been positive, some players and gaming streamers have reported glitches, crashes and unexpected behaviour during their initial sessions.
 
Discussions on gaming forums and social media have included reports of players getting stuck on loading screens, crashes during the opening missions, audio stuttering and occasional problems with character animations. Some PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S users have also reported issues with graphics rendering and gameplay progression.
 
Several clips showing unexpected in-game behaviour have circulated among gaming communities, adding to the discussion around the game's technical performance. However, these reports vary across platforms and individual player experiences, and there is not yet sufficient evidence to suggest a widespread technical failure.
 
Such problems are not uncommon when a large open-world game reaches millions of players. Even after extensive testing, certain glitches can emerge only when a much larger number of users begin interacting with the game across different hardware configurations and gameplay situations.
 
For Rockstar, the immediate challenge will be addressing recurring issues through patches and updates.

data.title: Can a housing society hike maintenance arbitrarily? Know your legal rights
data.description:
A housing society cannot arbitrarily raise monthly maintenance charges without explaining the reasons, backing the decision with expense records and following the prescribed approval process, legal experts say. A recent interim order by the Maharashtra State Co-operative Appellate Court has reinforced this principle, putting a steep maintenance hike on hold for two flat owners in Mumbai.
 
The dispute involved two residents of a housing society in Goregaon (West), whose monthly maintenance was raised from Rs 7,867 to Rs 27,166 and Rs 29,266, respectively, from July 2022. The society justified the increase by citing higher maintenance costs for their wing, which had only two flats.
 
 
The residents challenged the hike, arguing that the society had failed to follow the procedure for revising charges and that the calculation was unreasonable. On November 3, 2026, the appellate court granted interim relief, suspending the enhanced charges until the dispute is resolved.
 
The order is interim relief and does not amount to a final ruling that wing-wise maintenance charges are illegal.
 

Why did the court put the hike on hold?

The court found that the society had not demonstrated that it followed the process agreed upon at an earlier general body meeting. The meeting had proposed recalculating maintenance based on actual expenses, getting a chartered accountant to verify the figures, displaying the calculations and considering members' objections before finalising the charges.
 
The society, however, did not establish that these steps had been completed or that the revised charges had received the necessary general body approval before being implemented.
 
Tusi Kumar, partner at legal firm Singhania & Co., said a managing committee cannot impose disproportionate financial liabilities on members without a reasonable and legally sustainable basis. Any increase must be backed by actual expenditure, transparent calculations and compliance with applicable rules and bye-laws.
 
Manu Kumar Jha, associate, PSL Advocates & Solicitors, said maintenance increases must reflect actual cost escalation, with residents’ concerns considered before a decision is finalised.
 

Can a society charge different maintenance to different wings?

 
Housing societies can revise maintenance charges, but the calculation must follow applicable rules and bye-laws. Under the 2014 model bye-laws, service charges are generally apportioned equally among flats or units, while certain other expenses may be allocated differently depending on their nature.
 
Supriya Majumdar, partner, Elarra Law Offices, said maintenance revisions must be backed by proper expense calculations and approval at an annual or special general body meeting. A majority vote cannot justify an unreasonable financial demand on a minority of members.
 
Basudeb Biswas, advocate and real estate lawyer, said the society's authority to manage its affairs does not mean it can impose arbitrary charges. Residents must challenge the appropriate resolution or decision through the legal process.
 
Devishi Gupta, associate, SKV Law Offices, said residents are entitled to seek details of the revised calculations and question increases that are not adequately justified.
 
Aarya Bhat, advocate, Delhi High Court, said the order reinforces the principle that a numerical majority cannot use its voting power to impose arbitrary financial demands on a minority.
 

What should residents do if maintenance suddenly rises?

 
Flat owners facing a steep hike should:
 
  • Ask for a written breakdown of the revised maintenance charges, including the expenses used to calculate them.
  • Obtain meeting minutes and resolutions approving the increase, along with supporting records.
  • Check the registered bye-laws and applicable state rules to determine how individual expenses should be apportioned.
  • Raise objections in writing and, if necessary, approach the appropriate legal forum to challenge the decision.
 
Residents should not assume that challenging a hike automatically suspends payment obligations. Biswas said legitimate recurring maintenance dues remain recoverable, and residents should continue paying the undisputed amount while pursuing their challenge.

data.title: Delhi-NCR sees 25% growth in retail space leasing in Jan-Sep: JLL
data.description:
Leasing of retail spaces in shopping malls and high streets in Delhi-NCR rose 25 per cent to 2.47 million sq ft during the first nine months of this year on better demand from retailers, according to JLL.

Real estate consultant JLL India said that the gross leasing of retail space across seven major cities increased 5.6 per cent year-on-year to 9.36 million sq ft during January-September 2026 from 8.86 million sq ft in the year-ago period.

Delhi-NCR emerged as the leading market for nine-month gross leasing, accounting for a 26 per cent share, followed closely by Mumbai (25 per cent) and Bengaluru (21 per cent).

 

The consultant said that the total gross leasing in 2026 would surpass the 12.5 million sq ft recorded in 2025, supported by continued demand from both international and domestic retailers.

Commenting on the data, S K Sayal, MD & CEO of Bharti Real Estate, said, "Retail leasing in India is witnessing robust momentum, supported by strong fundamentals such as rising consumer confidence, evolving lifestyles, and the growth of experience-led formats.

In NCR, he said there is a growing preference for mixed-use marquee spaces that seamlessly blend retail, F&B, entertainment, and modern workspaces.

As per the data, the gross leasing in Mumbai rose 39 per cent to 2.31 million sq ft in the January-September period of this calendar year.

The gross leasing in Bengaluru fell 10 per cent to 2.01 million sq ft in the first nine months of this year. The demand fell 51 per cent in Hyderabad to 0.92 million sq ft.

In Chennai, the leasing increased 27 per cent to 0.57 million sq ft. The gross leasing grew 56 per cent in Kolkata to 0.75 million sq ft.

Lastly, the leasing in Pune increased 56 per cent annually to 0.33 million sq ft in the January-September 2026.

Robin Mangla, President of M3M India, said India's retail leasing activities reflect the growing strength and maturity of the country's retail real estate market.

"This momentum is being driven by evolving consumer preferences, the expansion of organised retail and the increasing demand for well-planned, experience-led retail destinations. Retail spaces are no longer limited to shopping; they are becoming vibrant social and lifestyle hubs that bring together shopping, dining and entertainment," he added.

Manish Periwal, Senior Vice President, Pioneer Urban, noted that Gurugram continues to be the first choice for brands seeking to expand in North India.

Shriram PM Monga, Co-founder of SRED Global, said, "Indian brands are expanding rapidly and account for the bulk of the space leased, while food and entertainment operators have become some of the biggest takers of space." Monga said the growth was restricted due to lack of quality supply.

"Vacancy in good malls is falling, rents in the best malls are firming up, and brands that cannot wait are moving to high streets," he added.

During the first nine months of 2026, shopping malls captured 45.9 per cent share of total gross leasing while high streets 46.3 per cent.

Among retailers, Fashion & Apparel segment took 31 per cent of retail space, followed by food & beverage 18 per cent and entertainment 15 per cent, the JLL data showed.

data.title: Sebi approves transfer of ICICI Securities' PMS biz to ICICI Prudential AMC
data.description:
Market regulator Sebi has approved the proposed transfer of portfolio management services (PMS) business of ICICI Securities to ICICI Prudential Asset Management Company.

The proposed acquisition will be carried out through a slump sale on a going-concern basis.

"We hereby inform you that the company is in receipt of an email today... from ICICI Securities intimating receipt of a letter dated November 19, 2026, from Securities and Exchange Board of India (Sebi) approving transfer of PMS business from ICICI Securities to the company," ICICI Prudential AMC said in a stock exchange filing on Thursday.

The company's board of directors approved the acquisition of the PMS business from ICICI Securities on August 10. Subsequently, both companies entered into a business transfer agreement for the transaction.

 

The closing of the transaction was subject to receipt of requisite regulatory approvals.

ICICI Prudential AMC said that further action in this regard would be taken in discussion with ICICI Securities.

The asset management firm reported a 6.1 per cent year-on-year rise in profit after tax (PAT) at Rs 889 crore for the September quarter of FY27 compared to ₹838 crore a year earlier, driven by higher revenue from operations.

Revenue from operations increased 16.3 per cent to ₹1,674 crore in the July-September quarter of FY27 compared to ₹1,439 crore in the year-ago period.

data.title: Six listed REITs distribute ₹3,234 crore in Q2 FY27 to 5.25 lakh investors
data.description:
India's six publicly listed Real Estate Investment Trusts (REITs) distributed a combined ₹3,234 crore to more than 5.25 lakh unitholders in the second quarter of FY27, according to data released by the Indian REITs Association. The distribution was nearly 39% higher than the ₹2,331 crore paid out in Q2 FY26, when five REITs were listed. In Q2 FY25, the four listed REITs distributed ₹1,383 crore.
 
The six listed trusts are Brookfield India Real Estate Trust, Embassy Office Parks REIT, Mindspace Business Parks REIT, Nexus Select Trust, Knowledge Realty Trust and Bagmane Prime Office REIT.
 
The sector's gross assets under management (AUM) stood at more than ₹3.30 lakh crore as of Q2 FY27. Its combined market capitalisation exceeded ₹2.09 lakh crore as of November 17, 2026.
 
 
Together, the six REITs manage more than 215 million sq ft of Grade A office and retail space across India. Since their inception, they have distributed more than ₹38,000 crore to unitholders.
 
The rise in quarterly distributions comes alongside an increase in the number of listed REITs. Knowledge Realty Trust and Bagmane Prime Office REIT have joined the four earlier listed trusts, expanding the range of listed property assets available to investors.
 
“The distribution of ₹3,234 crore during the quarter reflects the strength of India's REIT sector and its underlying assets,” said Shirish Godbole, chief executive officer of Knowledge Realty Trust and chairperson of the Indian REITs Association.
 
He said demand for office space from Global Capability Centres (GCCs) and front-office enterprises was supporting the sector. Healthy occupancy levels and rental collections, he added, were helping sustain distributions to investors.
 
REITs allow investors to gain exposure to income-generating commercial real estate without having to buy and manage an entire property. Investors purchase units listed on stock exchanges, while the trust owns and manages a portfolio of properties and distributes income to unitholders.
 
The quarterly distribution figure is an aggregate payout across the six trusts. It should not be confused with the return earned by an individual investor. The actual income received depends on the number of units held and the distribution declared by the particular REIT.
 
Investors should also distinguish between distributions and total returns. A REIT's total return includes both the income distributed and any change in the market price of its units. Unit prices can rise or fall with interest rates, property valuations, occupancy, rental growth and broader market conditions.
 
The distribution figure alone does not establish whether payouts have increased on a like-for-like basis across the trusts. The sector's expansion from four listed REITs in Q2 FY25 to six in Q2 FY27 also contributes to the increase in the aggregate amount distributed.
 
For investors evaluating REITs, factors such as occupancy, tenant concentration, lease expiries, debt levels, borrowing costs, rental escalations and the quality of the underlying properties remain important. Distributions are not fixed or guaranteed.
 
The Indian REITs Association, a non-profit industry body formed in 2023 under the guidance of the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI), represents the six listed trusts.
